transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-16 15:00 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Maria Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE), Lena Park (CTO, Nova Commerce), Rajat Singh (Head of ML), Amira Khalid (Platform Eng)

Summary:
Quick console walkthrough focusing on usage analytics, per-route dashboards, and cost breakdown. Customer wants clarity on per-route unit economics, how caching/batching affects bills, and options for dedicated vs hosted for production. Action items: pricing sheet, perf benchmark, security docs.

Topics:
- Console: per-route dashboards and drilldowns
- Cost breakdown: per-token, per-route, embeddings vs generation
- Caching & batching impact on unit costs
- Dedicated capacity / VPC / KMS and SOC2 concerns
- Next steps: pricing, benchmark, security materials

Transcript:
[00:00] Maria Chen: Hey everyone thanks for joining, I'm Maria from Redwood, I'm AE on this account, joining me is Diego from our SE team. How's everybody doing?
[00:05] Lena Park: Good thanks, excited to see the console. We had some questions from the deck you sent.
[00:10] Diego Alvarez: Great, we'll jump into the console and show the per-route dashboards. Quick note, apologies if auto-transcript mislabels some product names, I sometimes say "Redwood Dedicate" instead of "Redwood Dedicated" in the transcript, ha.
[00:20] Rajat Singh: Haha that's fine. Our main goal is understanding cost per route and how caching / batch settings change our monthly bill. We're running both embeddings for search and chat generation for assist.
[00:33] Maria Chen: Awesome. So first screen, top-level usage analytics. You can see total tokens, request counts, and latency percentiles over time. For Nova you're going to want to filter by model and by route — route being the API endpoint you define in the console.
[00:45] Amira Khalid: Can you show per-route cost breakdown? We have 12 routes in prod and a few internal ones.
[00:50] Diego Alvarez: Sure. (moves cursor) Here's the per-route dashboard. Each route shows tokens, requests, avg latency, and an estimated cost column. The cost column factors in model choice, quantization, and whether the route is hitting the KV prefix cache. Note the estimate uses our unit economics config — you can override with your committed pricing if you're on Dedicated.
[01:10] Maria Chen: There's also a toggle for 'Include caching savings' so you can compare raw cost vs after cache/batch optimizations.
[01:18] Rajat Singh: Hmm, how does the caching savings calculation work? Is it simulated or based on observed prefix hits?
[01:24] Diego Alvarez: It's based on observed prefix/KV hits in the last X days. We compute tokens saved by not re-sending cached prefixes and then multiply by the token price for that model. It's not perfect but gives a strong signal. We also surface the effective latency improvement.
[01:36] Lena Park: Does that reflect streaming responses / function-calling payload size? Our chat flows use function calls and return structured JSON often.
[01:43] Diego Alvarez: We annotate streaming vs non-streaming and will show token breakdown per field. Function call payloads are treated as tokens in/out; we show them separately in the route drilldown.
[01:52] Maria Chen: On server side we also show token split: prompt vs completion vs tool calls. That helps correlate which parts of the call are driving cost.
[02:00] Rajat Singh: Nice. About quantization — we saw in the model catalog you recommend different quantization profiles. How does that show up in the cost table?
[02:07] Diego Alvarez: Each model variant row includes a recommended quantization profile and an estimated throughput. The cost calculator lets you compare, for example, fp16 vs q4_0 vs q8_0 — we show latency and token cost delta and an estimated quality delta if you have evals.
[02:22] Amira Khalid: For compliance we need to know where logs and usage metrics live. Are analytics stored in your control plane or pushed to our VPC?
[02:29] Maria Chen: By default metrics live in Redwood's control plane with configurable retention. For Private/VPC deployments, metrics and traces can be configured to stay inside your VPC and we integrate with remote KMS for keys. We'll send the SOC2 and KMS docs after.
[02:41] Lena Park: Good. Another question: we use a mix of hosted and customers in europe — data residency matters. Does the per-route dashboard show region-level cost allocation?
[02:50] Diego Alvarez: Yes you can tag routes by region and we surface usage by region. If you route EU traffic to EU regions we show region-specific cost and latency. For private deployments you can pin routes to local clusters.
[03:02] Rajat Singh: On the cost breakdown UI, is the per-route 'estimated cost' near real-time? If we run a spike, can we see cost ramp up in 5-10 minutes?
[03:10] Diego Alvarez: Metrics are near real-time — typically 1-5 minute granularity depending on retention tier. You can also stream traces into your observability stack.
[03:17] Maria Chen: Let's open a sample route. (click) This route is our "search-embed" route — shows per-hour token histogram, cache hit ratio, batch sizes, and recommended batching window for throughput optimization.
[03:30] Amira Khalid: The recommended batching window: is that safe for latency-sensitive routes? We have routes with SLOs at 150ms tail.
[03:36] Diego Alvarez: Good point. The optimizer gives tiered recommendations: conservative (low latency), aggressive (max throughput). It simulates the latency distribution factoring in your p99 targets. For strict 150ms p95/p99 we usually recommend conservative batching or dedicated capacity.
[03:50] Rajat Singh: Dedicated capacity — can you remind us the difference in cost model vs hosted? We were thinking about a reserved pool vs pay-as-you-go.
[03:58] Maria Chen: Sure. Hosted is usage-based; you pay per-token and per-embedding unit. Dedicated is a monthly reserved capacity for GPU pools — you get predictable throughput and lower per-token effective costs when fully utilized. We also offer burst capacity for occasional spikes. We'll send the committed pricing examples.
[04:14] Lena Park: If we go Dedicated, what about private data — do we still see per-route analytics in the same Redwood console or do you provide a customer-hosted console?
[04:21] Diego Alvarez: With Private deployment we can run the control plane in your VPC; you get the same console UI but metrics stay inside your network if you choose. There's also an option for hybrid where metrics are mirrored to your observability.
[04:32] Maria Chen: Also want to call out rollouts and A/B testing in the console — you can split routes between model variants and see cost & quality side-by-side which is useful for deciding quantization vs model size.
[04:44] Rajat Singh: That's useful. A quick note on integrations: we use Datadog for infra metrics. Can Redwood push the per-route cost tags to Datadog?
[04:52] Diego Alvarez: Yes, we have a Datadog integration and can push metrics and tags. We also have a CSV export for cost reports if you want to import to your FinOps tools.
[05:00] Amira Khalid: On security — SSO, SAML, RBAC — we need role separation. Who in Redwood will be able to see our raw prompts in a hosted deployment?
[05:10] Maria Chen: By default, Redwood staff do not access customer prompts. Access is controlled via RBAC; in enterprise we enforce stricter access controls and can redact sensitive strings before storing. We'll include the audit log examples in the docs pack.
[05:22] Lena Park: Okay great. Back to cost: can you show an example of a cost-savings scenario with caching + batching?
[05:28] Diego Alvarez: Sure — here we have a 30-day window for a customer that implemented prefix caching and increased batching. Their per-token cost dropped by ~37% and CPU/GPU usage dropped in off-peak. The console shows the delta and projected monthly savings.
[05:40] Rajat Singh: And is that projection based on real observed distributions or a linear extrapolation?
[05:45] Diego Alvarez: It's based on observed distributions and a modeling layer that simulates how batching impacts throughput at your target latency. So it accounts for p50/p95/p99 skews, not just a linear scale.
[05:55] Maria Chen: Quick pause — any questions about API or SDK surface while we're here?
[06:00] Lena Park: We use Python and Node — are the SDKs supported for streaming and function calling?
[06:06] Diego Alvarez: Yes, both SDKs support streaming and function/tool calling. We also have examples for structured outputs and reranking.
[06:12] Rajat Singh: About benchmarking — we'd like Diego to run a benchmark simulating our traffic: mix of 60% embeddings, 40% chat, with 200ms target p95. Can we get that scheduled?
[06:22] Maria Chen: Absolutely, we'll coordinate. Diego, can you own the benchmark plan?
[06:26] Diego Alvarez: Yep I'll work with Rajat on the traffic profile and run a runbook; I'll share results and the raw metrics.
[06:31] Amira Khalid: Any limitations with private deployment for on-prem GPUs? We have a colocation policy for some customers.
[06:38] Diego Alvarez: On-prem is possible but depends on hardware compatibility; our runtime supports common GPU families and we provide a deployment guide. For truly air-gapped setups we have an enterprise packaging option.
[06:47] Maria Chen: Alright, to wrap up I'll recap next steps. We'll send the pricing and committed capacity doc, the SOC2/KMS/security whitepaper, and Maria will drop the private deployment README. Diego will schedule the perf benchmark with Rajat and run the tests.
[06:59] Lena Park: Sounds good. Could you also include a quick sample export of per-route CSV so our finance team can review?
[07:04] Maria Chen: Yup will include CSV export.
[07:08] Rajat Singh: Perfect, thanks all.
[07:11] Maria Chen: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up via email with dates and links.

End of call.
